title: Auditing Exposure to Harmful Content on TikTok using Multimodal Language Models: A Cross-National, Age-Stratified Study
abstract: arXiv:2608.17583v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Online video platforms can expose young users to harmful content, but independent audits remain difficult because video annotation is costly and moderation judgments vary across languages. We audit TikTok in France, Italy, and Sweden with sockpuppet accounts representing four age personas (13, 16, 19, 40), collecting 36,971 videos from passive For-You-page scrolling and active sessions that scroll, search for harm keywords, and scroll again. To scale annotation, we validate four multimodal LLMs against native-speaker labels on a 300-video reference set. Gemini 2.5 Flash with eight sampled frames plus text performs best (aggregate kappa = 0.42), at half the per-call cost of native-video upload, and we apply it to a 10% sample for approximately \$50 in total API spend across both modalities. translated_title: 使用多模态语言模型审计TikTok上有害内容的曝光：一项跨国、年龄分层研究
translated_abstract: 在线视频平台可能使年轻用户接触有害内容，但独立审计仍然困难，因为视频注释成本高昂，且不同语言的审核判断存在差异。我们在法国、意大利和瑞典对TikTok进行了审计，使用代表四种年龄角色（13岁、16岁、19岁、40岁）的傀儡账户，从被动“为你推荐”页面滚动和主动会话（滚动、搜索有害关键词并再次滚动）中收集了36,971个视频。为了扩展注释规模，我们验证了四种多模态LLM在300个视频参考集上对照母语标签的表现。Gemini 2.5 Flash配合八个采样帧和文本表现最佳（总体kappa=0.42），每次调用成本仅为原生视频上传的一半，我们将其应用于10%的样本，两种模态的总API花费约为50美元。关键词搜索返回35-56%的有害内容，在十二种国家-年龄组合中有十种比滚动基线增加了1.5-7.5倍；这一激增是...
tldr: 本研究通过多模态语言模型对TikTok进行跨国、年龄分层审计，发现关键词搜索显著增加有害内容曝光，且Gemini 2.5 Flash在成本效益上表现最佳。
en_tdlr: This study audits TikTok cross-nationally and by age using multimodal LLMs, finding keyword search significantly boosts harmful content exposure, with Gemini 2.5 Flash offering the best cost-effectiveness.
